# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 13

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 13 — Supporting Prophets (Firstfruits)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 4

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1-2: τροφή — "food" vs. "sustenance"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "worthy of his food" |
| LOGOS | "worthy of his sustenance" |
| PNEUMA | "deserves to be supported" |

**Issue:** τροφή = food/nourishment/sustenance. For a settled prophet, ongoing support rather than just meals is intended.
**Ruling:** "Worthy of his sustenance" (LOGOS) adopted. More comprehensive than "food" alone.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.3: ἀρχιερεῖς — "chief priests" vs. "high priests"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "chief priests" |
| LOGOS | "high priests" |
| PNEUMA | "high priests" |

**Issue:** ἀρχιερεῖς can refer to both the high priest specifically and the wider priestly aristocracy (chief priests). In the Didache context — where prophets are receiving the priestly firstfruits allocation — "high priests" better captures the Aaronic analogy.
**Ruling:** "High priests" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: listing produce items — order and coverage

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "produce of the winepress and the threshing floor, of oxen and sheep" |
| LOGOS | "produce of the wine-press and the threshing-floor, of cattle and sheep" |
| PNEUMA | "from the wine press, from the threshing floor, from your cattle and sheep" |

**Issue:** "Oxen" vs. "cattle" — βοῶν refers to cattle/oxen in general. "Cattle" is more natural English and broader.
**Ruling:** "Cattle and sheep" (LOGOS) adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.7: discretion clause — "as seems right" vs. "as seems appropriate"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "as seems right to you" |
| LOGOS | "as much as seems appropriate to you" |
| PNEUMA | "as seems right to you" |

**Issue:** ὡς ἂν σοι δόξῃ = as it seems to you / as you see fit. Both "right" and "appropriate" work; LOGOS adds "as much as" which is also in the Greek (specifying the quantity, not just the quality of discernment).
**Ruling:** "As much as seems appropriate to you" (LOGOS) adopted. The "as much as" is important — it addresses the quantity of the gift.
